We need a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions to target molecule: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1.

We have applied template 627376 gave precursors: CN1CCCC1=O (a lactam?) and COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2Cl)c1. So first disconnection: replace a chlorine on the triazine? Actually the product had Cl at position where original had N? The template seems to convert a chloro to amine? The retro step: from target, break amide? Actually template 627376 is a SN2-like where a chloride attached to aromatic heterocycle is replaced by amine (primary amine). So we get intermediate with Cl instead of NH2 on the heterocycle.

Now we need further disconnections to get to simpler precursors. The intermediate: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2Cl)c1.

We need to break amide maybe to get an acid chloride and amine? Or break the aryl-CO-N bond via Friedel-Crafts acylation? The guidance mentions Friedel-Crafts acylation (break halide, form carbonyl). Also substitution to replace OH with halogen.

We could consider disconnection of the amide: NC(=O) attached to aromatic ring. Could be formed via amide coupling of an aniline (the anisole ring) with a carboxylic acid (or acid chloride). So retro: break amide to give aniline (COc1cccc(NH2)c1) and acyl component (c2nnn(Cc3... )c2Cl)C(=O)Cl? Actually the amide is attached to the anisole ring via N. So we could propose amide formation from aniline and acid chloride of heterocycle.

Thus second step: target -> precursors: aniline (COc1cccc(NH2)c1) and acid chloride of heterocycle: ClC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3... )c2Cl? Wait the heterocycle currently has a Cl substituent on the triazine ring (c2nnn(... )c2Cl). The carbonyl attached to that heterocycle is attached to N of aniline. So the acyl component is (c2nnn(Cc3... )c2Cl)C(=O)Cl (acid chloride). So we need to generate that.

We can search for template that breaks amide to give acid chloride and amine. Use functional_groups_broken: amide, formed: acid chloride? Not in list. But we can break amide to give carboxylic acid and amine? The functional groups list includes "acyl chloride". So we could break amide to give acyl chloride and amine. Let's search.
